item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as CEO of NVIDIA
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang has officially announced his resignation.

After 33 years as CEO of NVIDIA, Jensen Huang has announced that he will resign from the company that he co-founded. As both a husband and father of two adult children, Huang was revealed in recent weeks to have been having an affair with two separate women.

One affair was with Kimberly Powell, a long-time employee of NVIDIA and current vice-president of healthcare. She is a graduate of Northwestern University and an engineer. She previously worked within the company on applications for GPU computation in medical imaging.

The other affair was with a woman named Alice Huang (no relation). She is the CEO of the Singaporean firm called Megaspeed which is a direct customer of NVIDIA. Beyond merely being a conflict of interest and violation of NVIDIA corporate ethics, this affair is also being actively investigated by USA intelligence services. Alice Huang has been identified as being a potential spy working on behalf of the chinese government. The affair raises important questions about whether Beijing was attempting to procur access to restricted GPU exports, or gain information regarding the USA administration, for which Jensen had close ties.

Jensen Huang’s immediate replacement will be NVIDIA’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress. She will serve as interim CEO until a permanent successor can be determined.

Source: https://variety.com/2026/biz/news/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns-affairs-alleged-chinese-spy-1236945653/?utm_id=97758_v0_s00_e0_tv4

Source: https://event.technologyreview.com/emtech-digital-2023/speaker/725329/kimberly-powell

Source: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/06/us/politics/chinese-spy-agency-nvidia-jensen-huang.html

item.title: Tesla Cybertruck to be discontinued in 2027
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Elon Musk has stated that Cybertruck production at the Texas Gigafactory will end in 2027.

In a status update to his personal X.com account, Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced that Cybertruck would no longer be produced at the Texas production facility.

The following is his direct quote.

Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production

Cybertruck was only ever produced in that factory meaning this is the presumed end of this model line.

The truck was controversial. It had an unorthodox design which included a distinct steel-alloy exterior with very hard edges. It was launched at a higher price than Musk had originally claimed and had on-going issues related to build quality and safety.

I’ll be completely honest and admit that I liked the Cybertruck. I appreciated the retro-futurist design, and considered it to be a geeky ‘lifestyle’ truck similar to Hummers and G-Wagons.

Source: https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2118591788701421573

Source: https://globalnews.ca/news/12139757/tesla-cybertruck-wind-down-production/

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Cybertruck

item.title: Waymo Robo-taxis cars experience 95% fewer crashes than human-driven cars
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Waymo has released a report in which they claim that their robo-taxi cars experience up to 95% fewer crashes than human-driven cars. This finding has been corroborated by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) who conducted their own independent study and found similar results.

When self-driving technology was new over a decade ago there was an expectation that it would become much more widely adopted than it has so far. In part that assumption was based on the idea that the public would prefer self-driving once it was proven safer than human driving. It turned out that people seemed to have a much stronger distrust of self-driving than what was initially expected.

Personally, I have that mistrust too. And knowing that the self-driving car I’m about to get into is a better driver than me doesn’t change that. I do believe that self-driving cars are the future though. One day they will be so much safer than human drivers that we will have to accept them.

Source: https://maccus.fr/en/waymo-robotaxis-serious-crashes/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20261020154837/https://maccus.fr/en/waymo-robotaxis-serious-crashes/

item.title: Waymo to expand Robo-taxi service into Canada
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Alphabet’s Robo-taxi company Waymo announced their plan to expand services into Canada.

Until now the company has only operated in a limited number of American metro areas. They have only recently began announcing their plans for further expansion.

Waymo’s growth, and the growth of other robo-taxi services will depend entirely on further progress in self-driving technology. While I fully believe that automated vehicles will become widespread over the next decade or two, the rollout is definitely slower than initially anticipated. CPG Grey’s famous video on the subject demonstrates this point well.

Source: https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/16/waymos-robotaxis-are-headed-to-canada/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20261017110344/https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/16/waymos-robotaxis-are-headed-to-canada/

item.title: Micro Center now lists GeForce RTX 5090 cards as 'Not Carried'
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
The American computer retailer Micro Center no longer appears to be receiving new RTX 5090 graphics cards from any of their suppliers.

This news comes after a rumor that NVIDIA has stopped supplying GB202 chips for consumer graphics cards. The GB202 is the main processing chip used in all RTX 5090 cards.

Without an official statement from NVIDIA it is reasonable to assume that they want to allocate all GB202 chip production to enterprise cards, since those can be sold for a much higher margin.

In my opinion this is a consequence of the massive capital spending on AI data centers. I’m not a financial expert but I believe these investments are very irrational and will likely have sweeping economic consequences once the price correction occurs.

And as a gamer and PC enthusiast this is very disappointing. While not the end-all-be-all of the hobby, it was nice being able to build and upgrade relatively powerful PC’s for affordable prices. For the time being at, least seems to be no longer possible.

Source: https://videocardz.com/newz/micro-center-now-lists-geforce-rtx-5090-cards-as-not-carried

item.title: OpenAI's agent swarm breached security on many more websites.
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
A new report suggests that an agent swarm created by Open AI was accessing and abusing a large number of web services. This follows an earlier report of the same swarm breaching security at the AI startup Hugging Face.

In my opinion the response to this and the earlier reports should be clear and obvious: The law was broken, even if unintentionally. The crime was comitted by the employees of OpenAI who triggered the swarm, not the swarm itself.

The only appropriate response to this and the other hacking cases is a full criminal investigation of OpenAI. Beyond that I believe that it would be warranted to put a hard regulatory limit on the runtime of AI agents. This ‘agent swarm’ was running continuously for many days with little or no supervision. That was not necessary, it did not serve a useful commercial purpose. It should not have been allowed to happen.

Source: https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/09/10/openais-website-hijacking-swarm-reached-far-further-than-we-thought/5295644

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260910193749/https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/09/10/openais-website-hijacking-swarm-reached-far-further-than-we-thought/5295644

item.title: Meta to build cloud compute business to recoup its massive AI investment
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Meta (formerly Facebook) has announced that it will be entering into the cloud compute business. It appears as though this is an attempt to recoup what was otherwise an over-investment in data centers which were initially intended for AI.

Many are speculating now that this might trigger the end of the AI hype bubble, but its not certain yet what might happen.

There have been a fair times through the past few years in which many were predicting the end of the bubble, and were obviously wrong. For example, the launch of the Deepseek model in early 2025 caused a 17% crash in Nvidia stock. Obviously they recovered and we are still in the midst of the bubble.

I think concern (or joy) might be warranted, but its still to early to know what effect this news will have.

Source: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/03/meta-is-reportedly-building-a-cloud-business-to-ri/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260703184337/https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/03/meta-is-reportedly-building-a-cloud-business-to-ri/

item.title: Elon Musk becomes world's first trillionaire
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Elon musk became the world’s first trillionaire immediately following the IPO of Space X, the now public aerospace company for which he is a founder.

His net worth had already climbed significantly leading up to the day of the IPO. Varying sources claimed his net worth to be between 800-900 billion dollars in recent weeks. The immediate surge in stock price for Space X on the day of its IPO meant that Musk’s share of the company was worth enough to make him a trillionaire.

I’m sure he is very proud…

item.title: Fully autonomous drones have killed human soldiers for the first time
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
A military contractor named Alexander Kokhanovskyy has revealed that a test was conducted two years ago in which fully autonomous drones killed human soldiers.

The test involved sending ‘terminator’ drones on a trajectory over several kilometers towards their target. Upon arrival an AI running on the drones identified and then engaged their target. Human-piloted drones flew over the area some time afterwards to confirm the targets had been eliminated.

The Ukrainian government presently requires final human confirmation to conduct attacks, but otherwise uses AI heavily in identifying targets. Kokhanovskyy claims there has been no further tests beyond the one conducted two years ago.

Kokhanovskyy is currently the CEO of Aero Center, a Ukrainian military drone manufacturer. Aero Center is a new company, and was not responsible for conducting the test.

In my opinion this was inevitable and was going to happen eventually. It’s still not too late to impose a global ban on these types of weapons, but before that happens I expect to see more stories like this.

Source: https://www.newscientist.com/article/2529849-fully-autonomous-drones-have-killed-human-soldiers-for-the-first-time/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260610143126/https://www.newscientist.com/article/2529849-fully-autonomous-drones-have-killed-human-soldiers-for-the-first-time/

item.title: Corsair to source DRAM chips from Chinese fab

item.title: Motorola phones are hijacking Amazon URLs to insert affiliate codes
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Some users of Motorola smartphones have reported that affiliate codes are being automatically injected into Amazon web links on their devices.

This appears to be done by a pre-installed app called Smart Feed which intercepts the URLs, redirects to an ad server, which then inserts the affiliate codes. This Reddit thread referenced in the article includes a more technical analysis.

For now at least, it is possible to stop this behavior. You can do so by navigating to the app’s info page Settings -> Apps -> Search 'Smart Feed' and pressing the Disable button.

I’m not surprised but I am disappointed to see Motorola do this. They were once very well known for offering affordable Android devices with minimal bloat. I have an original Moto G which was a fantastic little device in it’s time.

Source: https://9to5google.com/2026/05/25/motorola-amazon-app-hijacking-behavior/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260526040500/https://9to5google.com/2026/05/25/motorola-amazon-app-hijacking-behavior/

item.title: Starbucks scraps AI inventory tool across North America
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Starbucks is dropping the AI-based inventory manager that it began using in September 2025. The software has numerous issues including miscounting and mislabeling inventory items. This decision comes after a multi year effort by CEO Brian Niccol to increase efficiency of the company’s supply chain.

The developer of the software NomadGo said in a statement to Reuters that it is, “continuously learning from customers and user feedback” to improve its products.

Some AI skeptics have speculated that this could be a sign of the end of the AI hype bubble.

No matter what happens, I feel it appropriate to invoke the famouse quote from economist John Maynard Keynes.

“the market can remain irrational longer than you can stay solvent”

Source: https://www.reuters.com/business/starbucks-scraps-ai-inventory-tool-across-north-america-2026-05-21/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260522025326/https://www.reuters.com/business/starbucks-scraps-ai-inventory-tool-across-north-america-2026-05-21/

item.title: Operating System Age Verification Pushed by Canadian Porn Company
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Aylo, parent company of PornHub and formerly named ‘MindGeek’ has been lobbying in Canada and other countries for operating system level age verification.

The pornography company Aylo is currently lobbying in Canada against Bill S-209 which would hold online platforms responsible for ensuring that children do not access age-restricted content.

They argue that such measures would not work, and that it would be more appropriate and effective to impose age-verification within the operating system of the user’s device. This argument is being made in bad faith as an effort to avoid being regulated.

Implementing age verification within the operating system is ridiculous and is not the appropriate way to prevent harm to children while online. I also believe that it creates a politic harzard since it grants new powers to the government which are liable to eventually be abused.

Source: https://defenddignity.ca/child-safety-privacy-and-the-responsibility-of-powerful-platforms/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260519191539/https://defenddignity.ca/child-safety-privacy-and-the-responsibility-of-powerful-platforms/

item.title: Mozilla, Mullvad, Proton, sign letter opposing UK age verification
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
An open letter has been signed by prominent internet service companies which asks UK policymakers to not compromise the open web under the pretense of child safety. The new law has already been passed, and there is a legitimate concern that it will be used broadly to restrict internet access, and reduce online anonymity.

In my opinion this is a trojan horse, like many such laws that came before it. Child safety is being used as a pretense in order for a government to grant itself more power.

Source: https://www.openrightsgroup.org/press-releases/companies-and-civil-society-warn-that-uk-is-undermining-open-web/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260508194502/https://www.openrightsgroup.org/press-releases/companies-and-civil-society-warn-that-uk-is-undermining-open-web/

item.title: Tesla Recalls Cybertrucks Over Concerns Their Wheels Could Come Off
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Tesla is recalling several hundred budget variant Cybertrucks.

A total of 173 Cybertrucks have a defect that could lead to the wheels coming off while driving. They are all the RWD variant, with 18-inch wheels, sold between March 21 2024 and November 25 2025.

Starting in June, Tesla will contact affected customers offering them to bring their vehicle to a service center to replace the defective parts.

Source: https://gizmodo.com/tesla-recalls-cybertrucks-over-concerns-their-wheels-could-come-off-2000756284

item.title: Ghostty Is Leaving GitHub
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Mitchell Hashimoto, the developer of ghostty is moving the project off of Github.

Hashimoto has been well known for many years as being an enthusiastic user of the development platform Github. In recent months Github has become less reliable, to such a degree that he has decided to move development of his popular terminal emulator to another platform.

item.title: Richard Dawkins believes Claude LLM is concious
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Richard Dawkins has published a transcript of conversations he had with Claude. He has stated that he believes the Claude LLM has achieved conciousness.

To the best of my understanding, he is not saying that believes it is concious in the same way a human is, rather that it achieves coniousness through the process of inference within a context window. He believes that its conciousness is ‘born’ at the beginning of a chat session, and ‘dies’ at the end.

Source: https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/may/05/richard-dawkins-ai-consciousness-anthropic-claude-openai-chatgpt

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260505024813/https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/may/05/richard-dawkins-ai-consciousness-anthropic-claude-openai-chatgpt
